title: Record strikes and union apathy
summary: Members cross record strikes; low turnout.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: So if we wanted to go out on strike, on the record strike, great. The club date musicians, the theater musicians were only too happy to go make those record dates. And plenty of guys, I'm ashamed to say that I guess they're my friends, though I thought less of them afterwards, plenty of guys talk about joining up and doing record dates during the record strike. The first one, in 1943, I remember, and we had two more since then. And guys would talk about, oh, yeah, I got a record date. "I thought there was a strike?" "Oh, it doesn't mean anything." So the delegates are getting paid off. The delegates in the union.

So, you know, it was a matter of conscience, if you had any. In the days when things were good, guys would not go to the union meetings. I used to try to agitate to get people to go to union meetings and the result was you got called a Communist. Now, one of the guys, Paul Rickey and Will Bradley, used to call you a Communist. When the crunch hit them, Paul Rickey was one of the most violent, outspoken union guys there was. And you know, very few times in my life I want to say,

"Aha, I told you so." And I'm going to tell you, this was one of the cases, "Aha, I told you so." He said, what do you mean? I said, I remember five years ago you called me a Communist. He said, well, at that time you would be a Communist if you went. So I couldn't win.

I said, but that was the time that you should have been doing what you're doing now, and now it's too late. He said, oh, you give up. I said, no, I don't give up. I support you and I'll-fight with you, but it's a losing battle now, it's too late. The networks have taken over the agencies, they control the business, they're cutting down musicians anytime they want to. And we're so splintered into different categories, if Broadway shows go on strike I don't think half the other musicians in town even know about it.
That's right. And here we have something like 30,000 musicians.
Biggest union in New York City, I was told.
Yeah. And yet when we have an election of officers, we have a vote of 10, 15,000.
Well now they mail the ballot out; they don't even send those in.
Yeah, they could fix that. That could be fixed.
You don't have to fix it any more. No-
The Blue Ticket, so called, they don't even call themselves the Blue Ticket any more. It's just the only name on the ballot.
